newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drug chief to visit Thailand about heroin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug chief to visit Thailand about heroin.

text.p: The U.S. drug chief said on Friday he would meet officials in Thailand next week to discuss how to stem the flow of heroin from Southeast Asia.

Burma is the main source for most of the heroin reaching the United States from that region, White House Drug Policy Director Barry McCaffrey said, adding he hoped to gain insight from Thailand about its neighbour.
McCaffrey is scheduled to visit Thailand and Laos Nov. 21-26, and will accompany President Bill Clinton Nov. 26 to a meeting with Thailand Prime Minister Banharn Silpaarcha.
Thailand has been successful in dealing with the threat of drugs to its own population, McCaffrey told a media briefing.
The United States has 600,000 heroin addicts, and 60 percent of the heroin reaching its shores come from Southeast Asia, with Burma producing the "lion's share," he said.
He planned to visit opium production areas near the border with Burma in northwestern Thailand Nov. 23 and to visit Laos Nov. 24.
Heroin use in the United States has remained relatively stable, but recent data indicate heroin abuse is on the rise, McCaffrey's office said.

The failure of Burma to act effectively against its opium producers has led the United States to include it on the decertification list of countries not cooperating in efforts to combat drug trafficking, his office said.
